mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in the month prior to the prediction horizon is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-inflation periods (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 2.5% in the month prior.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightening reduces excess capacity and supports wage growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to beat a 5% benchmark in similar labor-market tightening regimes (p > 0.10), or UNRATE increases are not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) above their prior month's levels by at least 1% each, followed by a month of no change, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals strengthening business demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST ↑ ≥1% and GDPC1 ↑ ≥1% in the same month, followed by a month of flat growth
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the pattern, or the pattern recurs in contractionary regimes (e.g., during recessions).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index by more than 5% in the month prior to the prediction horizon, accompanied by a stable or rising CPIAUCSL (CPI), predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects supply-side contraction without broad price pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >5% in the prior month and CPIAUCSL does not fall >3% in the same month
regime_hint: Discretionary supply contraction in non-inflationary periods
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or CPIAUCSL declines by >3% alongside INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (reserves as a percent of GDP) over three consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates excess liquidity withdrawal and a potential shift toward growth-friendly policy.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 2% risk-free rate benchmark (p > 0.10), or RSAFS does not decline in three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior 12-month average, followed by two months of below-average employment, predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects a labor market overreaction and subsequent cooling.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS jumps >10% above prior 12-month average in a single month, then falls below average for two subsequent months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10), or the pattern is absent in non-crisis labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: A month-on-month acceleration in CPIAUCSL (CPI) growth rate by at least 0.3 percentage points above the prior month's rate predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals early inflationary pressure that is discounted by investors.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate accelerates by ≥0.3pp month-over-month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of similar CPI acceleration (p > 0.10), or CPIAUCSL growth does not accelerate.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side shock as indicated by a one-time drop in GDPC1 (goods orders) of at least 8% in a single month, with no prior such drop in the past 12 months, predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates production disruptions.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥8% in a single month and no prior ≥8% monthly drop in the past 12 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not underperform a supply-shock baseline (p > 0.10), or the shock pattern recurs in non-crisis periods.
